gaps.why_now: A dedicated Phase 11 build entry now keeps the landed gpio_wdt starter and the survey checkpoint reviewable together instead of letting the lane drift after the first driver scaffold landed.
The survey gate now acts as a freshness check around the landed gpio_wdt starter so the lane does not drift back to pre-driver assumptions or overclaim broader watchdog progress.

The survey note now records the landed gpio_wdt starter together with the bounded validation matrix, descriptor preflight checkpoint, timeout-property checkpoint, platform drvdata checkpoint, drvdata checkpoint, stop-policy split, teardown summary, registration handoff, register-device request surface, and the remaining registration, teardown, failure-mode, and hardware-backed validation work so the next Phase 11 step stays explicit without overstating broader watchdog progress.

The first gpio_wdt starter is now landed and models hw_algo parsing, heartbeat margin validation, bounded start or stop or ping transitions, a tiny probe-time summary, a descriptor preflight summary, a timeout-property checkpoint, a platform drvdata checkpoint summary, a drvdata checkpoint summary, a nowayout-aware stop helper, a registration-facing handoff summary, a register-device call summary, and a bounded teardown summary without touching live GPIO or platform registration.

Dedicated Phase 11 tests now keep the toggle and level state transitions, heartbeat validation, always-running stop behavior, nowayout-aware stop outcomes, descriptor preflight ordering, timeout-property checkpoint ordering, drvdata checkpoint ordering, pre-registration bookkeeping, teardown outcomes, registration handoff bookkeeping, and register-device request bookkeeping honest around the landed simple-driver scaffold.

A bounded slice note records exactly what the gpio_wdt starter, probe-summary helper, descriptor preflight helper, timeout-property checkpoint, platform drvdata checkpoint, drvdata checkpoint, stop-policy helper, registration handoff summary, and register-device call summary cover so later Phase 11 work can extend the model without reopening the starter contract.

A dedicated teardown note now keeps the bounded teardown ownership explicit by separating the stop-policy split, the stop transition, and the `teardownSummary()` handoff beside the starter so the review packet does not blur host-free teardown evidence into live GPIO, remove hooks, or reboot-backed shutdown behavior.

The bounded validation matrix now records the shared Phase 11 replay path, the exact focused survey replay, the current property, startup, descriptor-preflight, timeout-property, platform-drvdata, drvdata, runtime, stop-policy, handoff, register-device request, and teardown evidence, and the remaining registration, teardown, failure-mode, and hardware-backed validation gap so the review packet keeps one truthful validation posture.

The lane now lands a tiny probe-time summary for always-running startup, requested GPIO line mode, and watchdog-core-facing bookkeeping so the starter describes more of gpio_wdt_probe() before any live GPIO or platform glue.
The starter now lands a tiny nowayout-aware stop helper so review can distinguish watchdog-core stop blocking from hardware always-running behavior before any live GPIO or platform glue.

The starter now adds a tiny registration-facing handoff summary so review can see whether startup state, stop policy, timeout init, and reboot bookkeeping reach watchdog-core registration before any live GPIO or platform glue.

The starter now adds a tiny descriptor preflight summary so review can see the exact devm_gpiod_get() flag choice and the fact that descriptor lookup still sits before timeout parsing, always-running bookkeeping, and the registration-facing handoff without claiming live GPIO acquisition.

The starter now adds a tiny timeout-property checkpoint so review can see that hw_margin_ms stays required and bounds-checked after descriptor lookup but before always-running bookkeeping, watchdog_set_drvdata(), and the registration-facing handoff, while invalid timeout values still block those later handoffs.

The starter now adds a tiny platform drvdata checkpoint summary so review can see that the probe-time allocation is followed by platform_set_drvdata() before hw_algo parsing, descriptor lookup, hw_margin_ms validation, and the later watchdog_set_drvdata()/registration handoffs without claiming live platform probing.
A focused Phase 11 harness now keeps the early platform_set_drvdata() ordering explicit around the landed checkpoint without widening into the broader shared Phase 11 build packet.

The starter now adds a tiny drvdata checkpoint summary so review can see that descriptor lookup and the required hw_margin_ms property still precede watchdog_set_drvdata(), and that the drvdata handoff itself stays required before both the registration-facing handoff and the first register-device request surface without claiming live GPIO or platform registration.

The starter now adds a tiny register-device call summary so review can see the first bounded devm_watchdog_register_device() request surface, including descriptor readiness, watchdog_set_drvdata() completion, timeout propagation, and the still-blocked live GPIO, platform-registration, and reboot-glue boundaries without claiming execution.

Platform-driver registration, GPIO descriptor acquisition, watchdog_set_drvdata() execution, watchdog core registration, teardown and failure-mode parity, and hardware-backed validation remain blocked until the lane grows a real registration-facing scaffold that bridges the landed summaries to live GPIO and watchdog-core execution.
